title: Local Seismic Event and Noise-Floor Separation
dataSources: Seismograph events (`seismograph:event`), seismic noise (`seismograph:noise`), air quality (`airquality:reading`), radiation counts (`radiation:count`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), phenology observations (`phenology:observation`), and weather-station rainfall (`weatherstation:reading`).
app: Citizen-science telemetry from seismographs, weather stations, air-quality monitors, Geiger counters, lightning feeds, and phenology journals streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=seismograph:event
| stats count as events avg(signal_to_noise_db) as avg_snr_db by classification
| sort - events
description: Separates probable local quakes, regional events, and plain noise so your backyard seismograph becomes easier to interpret.
value: Raw event counts are noisy; grouping by classification makes the sensor far more useful for hobby science and tuning.
implementation: Ingest event classifications from Raspberry Shake or your own classifier alongside signal-to-noise values.
visualization: Bar chart of event counts by classification with average SNR.
grandmaExplanation: It spots which shakes looked like real events and which were just background rumble, so your seismograph logs make more sense.
